findings.title: Unauthenticated SQL injection in user lookup
findings.evidence: return db.execute("SELECT id FROM users WHERE name = '" + name + "'").fetchall()
findings.explanation: The name value comes from an unauthenticated HTTP request and is concatenated directly into SQL. An attacker can supply ' OR '1'='1 to change the WHERE clause and retrieve all user IDs.
findings.recommendation: Use a parameterized query and pass name as a bound parameter using the database driver's supported placeholder syntax.
findings.suggested_test: Pass ' OR '1'='1 as name and assert that it is treated as a literal name and does not return unrelated users.

findings.title: Unauthenticated input is concatenated into SQL
findings.evidence: return db.execute("SELECT id FROM users WHERE name = '" + name + "'").fetchall()
findings.explanation: The name parameter comes from an unauthenticated HTTP request and is inserted directly into SQL. A value such as ' OR '1'='1 changes the WHERE clause to return every user ID instead of matching one name.
findings.recommendation: Use a parameterized query with the database driver's placeholder syntax and pass name separately as a bound parameter.
findings.suggested_test:
Pass ' OR '1'='1 as name and assert it is treated as a literal name and does not return unrelated users.
Seed users named alice and bob, then call find_user with name "' OR '1'='1". Assert no rows are returned and the input is passed as a bound parameter. Also assert that an existing name containing an apostrophe is matched correctly.
